docs.title: What is coursebook?
docs.text: coursebook turns a folder of markdown files into the materials for a course or publication: a Word, PDF, or HTML document with the text, a PowerPoint deck with accompanying slides, and a document of teaching notes. You write each part of your project once, in plain markdown, with its text, slides, and notes side by side. A short project file sets the order of the parts and how the results should look.

docs.title: Why use coursebook?
docs.text:
• One source for everything: the text, slides, and notes for each chapter or section live in the same markdown file, so they stay in sync.
  • Outlines you already know: the structure of a project is a traditional outline (I, A, 1, a, i). Headings and their levels come from it.
  • Microsoft Office output: Word and PowerPoint files are styled with templates, including Word (.docx, .dotx) and PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx) templates and Office themes (.thmx).
  • PDF and HTML too: the text and notes can also be exported to PDF (without LaTeX) and to a single, self-contained HTML file, at the same time as Word.
  • Academic features: footnotes, citations from BibTeX or other bibliography files (with Bluebook citations for law reviews), tables, math, and images, all through pandoc.
  • Styles for academic work: built-in styles for coursebooks, books, and law review articles, and an easy way to add your own.
  • Nothing else to install: a copy of pandoc is included.

coursebook is not a word processor. If you need tracked changes or comments from co-authors, export with coursebook and continue in Word.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: coursebook requires Python 3.11 or later and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Any text editor works for writing the markdown files.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install coursebook, use pip:

pip install coursebook

PDF export needs one more package, which this installs:

pip install "coursebook[pdf]"

docs.title: Starting a project
docs.text:
coursebook new creates a project folder with a project file, a source file for each outline entry, and a "visuals" folder:

coursebook new my_course --style coursebook --entry "I: Introduction" --entry "II: Negligence"

Instead of --entry, you can pass --outline outline.txt, a text file with one outline line per line. Use --format toml or --format yaml for a toml or yaml project file. Without an outline, a short sample outline is used. Existing source files are never overwritten.

docs.title: Project folders
docs.text:
A project is a folder with a project file, one markdown file for each entry in the outline, and (optionally) a "visuals" folder with images:

my_course/
├── project.ini
├── introduction.md
├── literature_review.md
├── ...
└── visuals/
    └── chart.png

docs.title: The project file
docs.text:
The project file is named "project" and may be an ini, toml, or yaml file. Its "Project" section holds settings and its "Outline" section holds the structure of the project:

[Project]
Name: Crazy Idea
Author: Corey Rayburn Yung
Style: coursebook
Include: text, slides, notes
Slides Template: chalkboard
Output Folder: output

[Outline]
I: Introduction
II: Literature Review
III: My Cool Idea
A: Interesting Premise 1
1: Underlying Facts
2: Supporting Work
B: Interesting Premise 2
IV: Conclusion

The level of each outline entry comes from its label: upper case Roman numerals (I), upper case letters (A), numbers (1), lower case letters (a), and lower case Roman numerals (i), in whatever order you nest them. A book can number its chapters with "1", "2", and so on. Labels may repeat under different parents (an "A" under "I" and another under "II"). If you skip a label (such as going from "A" to "C"), coursebook warns you but keeps going. After "h", an "i" continues the letters.

Entries without numbers, such as a preface or an appendix, use dashes as their labels: - for the top level, -- for the level below it, and so on. The numbering of the other entries continues around them:

[Outline]
-: Preface
I: Introduction
II: Argument
-: Appendix
A: Data

An entry can name its own source file after a |, which is useful for files in subfolders or for entries that share a title:

I: Introduction | chapters/intro.md
A: Overview | intro_overview.md
II: Negligence
A: Overview | negligence_overview.md

In a toml or yaml file, the outline is a list (of lines or of [label, title, file] lists):

outline = [
    "I: Introduction",
    "II: Background",
    "A: History",
    "B: Current Law"]

[project]
name = "A Modest Proposal"
style = "law review"

docs.title: Source files
docs.text:
Each outline entry is matched to a markdown file named after its title, in lower case with underscores for spaces and punctuation ("Interesting Premise 1" matches "interesting_premise_1.md"). An entry without a file still gets a heading, and coursebook warns you that the file is missing.

A source file is divided into sections by lines with the section name in angle brackets. Anything before the first divider is text:

---
title: A Better Title Than the Outline's
visuals_in_notes: true
---

The text of the chapter, with a footnote.[^1]

# A Subheading

![Enrollment by year](chart.png){width=50%}

[^1]: Footnote labels only need to be unique within each file.

<slides>

# First Slide

- A point
- Another point

::: notes
Speaker notes for this slide.
:::

---

- A second slide, without a title

<notes>

Notes for the instructor's guide.
  • Front matter (optional) may set title (used in place of the outline title) and visuals_in_notes.
  • Text: write headings starting at #. They are placed beneath the heading for the outline entry.
  • Slides: start each slide with a # heading or separate slides with ---. If the slides do not start with a heading, the first slide is titled with the outline entry. Speaker notes go in notes blocks.
  • Notes: like the text, but collected into a separate document. Entries without notes are left out of it.
  • Images are found in the project folder and the visuals folder.
  • Citations use pandoc's syntax ([@scalia1997, 23]) when the project has a bibliography. With a note style, such as the Bluebook style used by law review, each citation becomes a footnote.

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
From the project folder, run:

coursebook

Or name the folder and choose the sections to create:

coursebook path/to/my_course --include slides --output-folder handouts

(coursebook build is the same command, and python -m coursebook works too.) For the project above, coursebook creates "crazy_idea.docx", "crazy_idea_slides.pptx", and "crazy_idea_notes.docx" in the output folder. With Text Format: word, pdf, html, it also creates "crazy_idea.pdf" and "crazy_idea.html".

When you open a Word document with a table of contents, Word asks whether to update the fields in it; answer yes to fill in the table. PDF files use the fonts installed on your computer, so a missing font (such as Georgia on some Linux systems) is replaced with another one.

docs.text:
Style Sections Headings Formatting coursebook text, slides, notes titles, table of contents Georgia, 11 point, page numbers book text, slides titles, table of contents Georgia, 11 point, page numbers law review text, slides labels ("I. Introduction"), centered and capitalized Times New Roman, 12 point, double spaced, 10 point footnotes, one inch margins, page numbers, Bluebook citations

A style's formatting is applied to pandoc's default Word template and passed to the PDF and HTML files. If you name your own Word template, its formatting is used for Word files instead.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
A template setting may be a path (relative to the project folder) or a name without an extension. A name is looked for first in the project folder and then among the templates included with coursebook ("chalkboard"). Word accepts .docx and .dotx files, and PowerPoint accepts .pptx and .potx files and .thmx Office themes. A PowerPoint template must have the standard layouts (Title Slide, Title and Content, Section Header, Two Content, Comparison, Content with Caption, and Blank).

To start your own template from a style's, write it out, change it in Word or PowerPoint, and name it in the project file:

coursebook template "law review" house_style.docx
coursebook template coursebook lecture.pptx

Text Template: house_style
Slides Template: lecture

The CSL setting works the same way: it may be a path to a .csl file or the name of one, looked for in the project folder and then among the citation styles included with coursebook ("bluebook-law-review"). Thousands of citation styles are available from the Zotero Style Repository.

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import coursebook

project = coursebook.Project.from_folder('my_course')
print(project.missing)            # outline entries without a source file
print(project.assemble('slides')) # the combined markdown for the slides
project.build(include = ['text'])

New styles and export formats are registered when you subclass coursebook.Style or coursebook.Exporter:

import dataclasses

import coursebook


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Seminar(coursebook.Coursebook):
    number_headings: bool = True
    formatting: coursebook.Formatting = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory = lambda: coursebook.Formatting(
            body_font = 'Garamond', font_size = 12, page_numbers = True))

A project file can then use Style: seminar.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

• Renamed the package from cento to coursebook (the cento name is taken on PyPI).
  • Updated the repository to the latest snickerdoodle template: uv and hatchling replace PDM, and CI runs the tests, pre-commit, ruff, mypy, Codecov, and the documentation build.
  • Added the coursebook command (also python -m coursebook), with build (the default) to create a project's files, new to create a project folder with a project file and source files, and template to write a style's Word or PowerPoint template for editing.
  • Added project files in ini, toml, and yaml formats. Outlines may repeat labels under different parents, and each entry's level comes from its label (I, A, 1, a, i). Entries may be unnumbered (-: Preface) and may name their own source files (I: Introduction | chapters/intro.md).
  • Added source files with YAML front matter and <text>, <slides>, and <notes> sections.
  • Added Word export for the text and notes and PowerPoint export for the slides, using a bundled copy of pandoc.
  • Added PDF export (with Typst, through the pdf extra) and single-file HTML export for the text and notes. Each section may be exported to more than one format at once.
  • Added the coursebook, book, and law review styles, which set headings, the table of contents, the citation style, and the formatting of Word, PDF, and HTML files (including margins and page numbers).
  • Added the Bluebook law review citation style, which law review uses to turn citations into footnotes.
  • Added Word (.docx, .dotx) and PowerPoint (.pptx, .potx, .thmx) templates, including the bundled "chalkboard" theme.
  • Added footnotes that stay separate across source files (and are numbered continuously, including in LibreOffice), citations from bibliography files, images from a visuals folder, and speaker notes.

docs.title: Environment Setup
docs.text:
Install uv, then create a virtual environment with all of the development dependencies from the repository folder:

uv sync

Then, install the pre-commit hooks so that they run before each commit:

uv run pre-commit install

Run the tests with uv run pytest.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Follow this basic process:

  1. Fork and clone the repository.
  2. Create a new branch: git checkout -b feature-or-bugfix-name.
  3. Edit the code.
  4. If you added functionality or features, update the documentation accordingly.

If you are unsure about how to fix or ignore a warning, just let the continuous integration fail, and we will help you during review.

Don't bother updating the changelog, we will take care of this.

docs.title: Pull requests guidelines
docs.text:
Link to any related issue in the Pull Request message.

During the review, we recommend using fixups:

# SHA is the SHA of the commit you want to fix
git commit --fixup=SHA

Once all the changes are approved, you can squash your commits:

git rebase -i --autosquash main

And force-push:

git push -f

If this seems all too complicated, you can push or force-push each new commit, and we will squash them ourselves if needed, before merging.

docs.title: Style Guidelines
docs.text:
This package follows the Google Python Style Guide with two notable exceptions:

  1. It always adds spaces around "=". This not only violates the Google guide, it violates PEP8, the foundational Python style guide from which all other resources are derived. I defy this strong, long-standing norm because I find it more readable. My brain and eyes have trouble seeing two separate objects when an equal sign is in the middle. I imagine that I am not alone in this accessibility issue. Further, as PEP8 itself notes, required spaces around equal signs are becoming increasing common with type annotations becoming part of best practices (and, as a result, signatures to classes, functions, and methods regularly include spaces around the equal signs). I realize that this will seem alien to many coders, but it is far easier on my eyes.
  2. I use some so-called "power features", primarily dunder methods, to make my interfaces easier to access and use. This is disfavored in the Google Python Style Guide because such code is often more difficult for others to read. To address that concern, I try to document and comment as to what the code is doing whenever I used any of the "power features" of Python.

Because of the first exception, the project does not use a code formatter (such as ruff format), which would remove those spaces.

def export(
        self,
        text: str,
        path: pathlib.Path,
        options: ExportOptions | None = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Exports markdown `text` to the file at `path`.

    Args:
        text: pandoc markdown.
        path: path for the exported file.
        options: export options. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
            defaults of `ExportOptions`.

    Returns:
        The path to the exported file.

    """
    options = options or ExportOptions()
    text = _add_metadata(text, self.get_metadata(options))
    pypandoc.convert_text(
        text,
        to = self.pandoc_format,
        format = 'markdown',
        outputfile = str(path),
        extra_args = self.get_arguments(options))
    return path

def get_arguments(self, options: ExportOptions) -> list[str]:
    """Returns the pandoc command line arguments for `options`.

    Args:
        options: export options.

    Returns:
        The arguments to pass to pandoc.

    """
    arguments: list[str] = []
    if options.template is not None:
        arguments.append(f'--reference-doc={options.template}')
    if options.resource_paths:
        folders = _list_paths(options.resource_paths)
        arguments.append(f'--resource-path={folders}')
    if options.bibliography:
        arguments.append('--citeproc')
        arguments.extend(
            f'--bibliography={path}' for path in options.bibliography)
        if options.csl is not None:
            arguments.append(f'--csl={options.csl}')
    return arguments

@classmethod
def from_lines(cls, lines: Iterable[OutlineLine]) -> Outline:
    """Creates an outline from labeled lines.

    Args:
        lines: each item is either a line from an outline (such as
            'A: History') or a `tuple` of a label, a title, and
            (optionally) a file. Blank lines are skipped.

    Returns:
        An outline with the level of each entry set from its label.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a line has no label or title, or if a label cannot
            be placed in the outline.

    """
    outline = cls()
    # The last item is the most recent entry.
    stack: _Stack = []
    for line in lines:
        if isinstance(line, str):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            label, title, file = parse_outline_line(line)
        else:
            label, title, file = _parse_parts(line)
        if _is_unnumbered(label):
            depth, kind, number = _place_unnumbered(label, title, stack)
            label = ''
        else:
            depth, kind, number = _place_label(label, stack)
        entry = OutlineEntry(
            label = label, title = title, level = depth, file = file)
        del stack[depth:]
        if depth == 0:
            outline.entries.append(entry)
        else:
            stack[-1][0].children.append(entry)
        stack.append((entry, kind, number))
    return outline

def export(
        self,
        text: str,
        path: pathlib.Path,
        options: ExportOptions | None = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Exports markdown `text` to the PDF file at `path`.

    Args:
        text: pandoc markdown.
        path: path for the exported file.
        options: export options. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
            defaults of `ExportOptions`.

    Returns:
        The path to the exported file.

    Raises:
        ImportError: if the `typst` package is not installed.

    """
    try:
        import typst  # noqa: PLC0415
    except ImportError as error:
        message = (
            'PDF export needs the "typst" package (install it with '
            'pip install "coursebook[pdf]")')
        raise ImportError(message) from error
    options = options or ExportOptions()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        folder = pathlib.Path(temporary)
        source = folder / 'document.typ'
        # Pandoc runs in the temporary folder so that the images it copies
        # there have paths that Typst can find.
        pypandoc.convert_text(
            _add_metadata(text, self.get_metadata(options)),
            to = self.pandoc_format,
            format = 'markdown',
            outputfile = str(source),
            extra_args = self.get_arguments(options),
            cworkdir = temporary)
        typst.compile(str(source), output = str(path), root = temporary)
    return path

def build(
        self,
        include: Iterable[str] | None = None,
        output_folder: _PathLike | None = None) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Creates the files for the sections of the project.

    Each section is exported to every format set for it (such as Word and
    PDF). The files are exported at the same time, each in its own pandoc
    process.

    Args:
        include: the sections to create files for. Defaults to `None`,
            which uses `include`.
        output_folder: folder for the created files. Defaults to `None`,
            which uses `output_folder`.

    Returns:
        The paths to the created files, in the order of `include` and then
            of the formats of each section.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if a template, bibliography, or CSL file is not
            found.
        ImportError: if a format needs a package that is not installed.
        ValueError: if a section, format, or template is not valid, or a
            format cannot hold a section.
        RuntimeError: if pandoc fails.

    """
    sections = settings.normalize_sections(
        self.include if include is None else include)
    folder = (
        self.output_folder if output_folder is None
        else self._resolve(output_folder))
    for entry in self.missing:
        _LOGGER.warning(
            'No source file "%s" for outline entry "%s"',
            entry.file_name, entry.title)
    folder.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    stem = markdown.normalize_name(self.settings.name) or 'coursebook'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        jobs = []
        for section in sections:
            text = self.assemble(section)
            for name in self.settings.formats_for(section):
                exporter = exporters.get_exporter(name)
                if section not in exporter.sections:
                    message = (
                        f'the {section} cannot be exported to {name} '
                        f'(use {", ".join(_formats_for(section))})')
                    raise ValueError(message)
                options = self._get_options(
                    section, exporter, pathlib.Path(temporary))
                path = folder / (
                    f'{stem}{_SUFFIXES[section]}.{exporter.extension}')
                jobs.append((exporter, text, path, options))
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool:
            futures = [pool.submit(job[0].export, *job[1:]) for job in jobs]
            return [future.result() for future in futures]

        outline = project_outline,
        sources = project_sources,
        style = style)

def get_exporter(name: str) -> Exporter:
    """Returns the exporter with `name`.

    Args:
        name: the name of an `Exporter` subclass or one of its aliases (such as
            'word' or 'PowerPoint').

    Returns:
        An instance of the exporter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no exporter has `name`.

    """
    key = markdown.normalize_name(name)
    choices: dict[str, type[Exporter]] = {}
    for registered_name, registered in Exporter.registry.items():
        choices[str(registered_name)] = registered
        for alias in registered.aliases:
            choices.setdefault(alias, registered)
    choices.pop('exporter', None)
    if key not in choices:
        known = ', '.join(sorted(
            alias for exporter in choices.values()
            for alias in exporter.aliases))
        message = f'unknown format "{name}" (use one of: {known})'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return choices[key]()

Combines the source files of a project into a single markdown document.

The outline sets the order of the source files and adds a heading for each entry. The headings inside each source file are moved beneath the heading of its entry, and its footnote labels are made unique so that footnotes from different files do not collide.

def assemble_document(
        project_outline: outline.Outline,
        project_sources: Mapping[str, sources.Source],
        *,
        section: str,
        style: styles.Style,
        include_empty: bool = True,
        visuals_in_notes: bool = False) -> str:
    """Combines one section of every source into a markdown document.

    Each outline entry becomes a heading at the level of the entry (so a top
    level entry is a level one heading). The headings in each source are
    moved beneath the heading of its entry.

    Args:
        project_outline: the outline of the project.
        project_sources: the sources of the project, with keys that are the
            names of the outline entries.
        section: the section to combine ('text' or 'notes').
        style: the style of the project.
        include_empty: whether to add headings for entries that have no
            content in `section` (and no entries beneath them with content).
            Defaults to `True`.
        visuals_in_notes: whether to copy the images in the text of each
            source into its notes when `section` is 'notes'. A source's front
            matter may override this. Defaults to `False`.

    Returns:
        The combined markdown.

    """
    parts: list[str] = []
    for entry in project_outline.walk():
        if not include_empty and not _has_content(
                entry, project_sources, section, visuals_in_notes):
            continue
        source = project_sources.get(entry.name)
        level = min(entry.level + 1, _MAXIMUM_HEADING_LEVEL)
        heading = style.format_heading(_titled(entry, source))
        parts.append(f'{"#" * level} {heading}')
        body = _get_body(source, section, visuals_in_notes)
        if body:
            body = markdown.namespace_footnotes(body, prefix = entry.name)
            parts.append(markdown.shift_headings(body, levels = level))
    return _join(parts)

def assemble_slides(
        project_outline: outline.Outline,
        project_sources: Mapping[str, sources.Source],
        *,
        style: styles.Style,
        section_slides: bool = True) -> str:
    """Combines the slides of every source into a markdown slide deck.

    The deck uses pandoc's slide level 2: each level two heading (or
    horizontal rule) starts a new slide and each level one heading is a
    section title slide. In a source file, each slide starts with a level one
    heading (which becomes level two) or a horizontal rule ('---'). If the
    slides of a source do not start with a heading, the first slide is given
    the heading of its entry.

    Args:
        project_outline: the outline of the project.
        project_sources: the sources of the project, with keys that are the
            names of the outline entries.
        style: the style of the project.
        section_slides: whether to add a section title slide for each entry
            that has slides (or entries beneath it with slides). Defaults to
            `True`.

    Returns:
        The combined markdown.

    """
    parts: list[str] = []
    for entry in project_outline.walk():
        if not _has_content(entry, project_sources, 'slides'):
            continue
        source = project_sources.get(entry.name)
        heading = style.format_heading(_titled(entry, source))
        if section_slides:
            parts.append(f'# {heading}')
        body = _get_body(source, 'slides')
        if body:
            if not body.lstrip().startswith('#'):
                parts.append(f'## {heading}')
            body = markdown.namespace_footnotes(body, prefix = entry.name)
            parts.append(markdown.shift_headings(body, levels = 1))
    return _join(parts)

def main(arguments: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Runs a command from the command line.

    If the first argument is not a command, the command is 'build'.

    Args:
        arguments: the command line arguments, without the program name.
            Defaults to `None`, which uses `sys.argv`.

    Returns:
        The exit status: 0 if the command succeeded and 1 otherwise.

    """
    values = list(sys.argv[1:] if arguments is None else arguments)
    if not values or values[0] not in {*_COMMANDS, '-h', '--help', '--version'}:
        values.insert(0, 'build')
    options = _create_parser().parse_args(values)
    logging.basicConfig(
        format = '%(levelname)s: %(message)s',
        level = (
            logging.INFO if getattr(options, 'verbose', False)
            else logging.WARNING))
    try:
        if options.command == 'new':
            paths = _new(options)
        elif options.command == 'template':
            paths = [scaffold.write_template(
                options.style, options.destination)]
        else:
            paths = _build(options)
    except (ImportError, OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'coursebook: error: {error}\n')
        return 1
    for path in paths:
        sys.stdout.write(f'Created {path}\n')
    return 0

def export(
        self,
        text: str,
        path: pathlib.Path,
        options: ExportOptions | None = None) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Exports markdown `text` to the PDF file at `path`.

    Args:
        text: pandoc markdown.
        path: path for the exported file.
        options: export options. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
            defaults of `ExportOptions`.

    Returns:
        The path to the exported file.

    Raises:
        ImportError: if the `typst` package is not installed.

    """
    try:
        import typst  # noqa: PLC0415
    except ImportError as error:
        message = (
            'PDF export needs the "typst" package (install it with '
            'pip install "coursebook[pdf]")')
        raise ImportError(message) from error
    options = options or ExportOptions()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        folder = pathlib.Path(temporary)
        source = folder / 'document.typ'
        # Pandoc runs in the temporary folder so that the images it copies
        # there have paths that Typst can find.
        pypandoc.convert_text(
            _add_metadata(text, self.get_metadata(options)),
            to = self.pandoc_format,
            format = 'markdown',
            outputfile = str(source),
            extra_args = self.get_arguments(options),
            cworkdir = temporary)
        typst.compile(str(source), output = str(path), root = temporary)
    return path

def get_exporter(name: str) -> Exporter:
    """Returns the exporter with `name`.

    Args:
        name: the name of an `Exporter` subclass or one of its aliases (such as
            'word' or 'PowerPoint').

    Returns:
        An instance of the exporter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no exporter has `name`.

    """
    key = markdown.normalize_name(name)
    choices: dict[str, type[Exporter]] = {}
    for registered_name, registered in Exporter.registry.items():
        choices[str(registered_name)] = registered
        for alias in registered.aliases:
            choices.setdefault(alias, registered)
    choices.pop('exporter', None)
    if key not in choices:
        known = ', '.join(sorted(
            alias for exporter in choices.values()
            for alias in exporter.aliases))
        message = f'unknown format "{name}" (use one of: {known})'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return choices[key]()

def namespace_footnotes(text: str, prefix: str) -> str:
    """Adds `prefix` to the footnote labels in markdown `text`.

    Pandoc treats footnote labels as belonging to the whole document. So, if two
    source files each use `[^1]`, the second footnote would be replaced by the
    first when the files are combined. Adding a prefix that is unique to each
    source file keeps the footnotes separate.

        prefix: text to add to the start of each footnote label.

            definitions) changed from `[^label]` to `[^prefix-label]`.

    lines = []

        lines.append(
            line if in_code else _FOOTNOTE.sub(rf'[^{prefix}-\1]', line))

def shift_headings(text: str, levels: int) -> str:
    """Changes the level of every heading in markdown `text`.

    Only ATX headings (headings that start with '#') are changed. Headings
    inside fenced code blocks are left alone. Markdown does not support more
    than six levels of headings, so deeper headings are kept at level six.

    Args:
        text: markdown text.
        levels: number of levels to add to each heading. A negative number
            raises the headings, but never above level one.

    Returns:
        `text` with its headings shifted.

    """
    lines = []
    for line, in_code in _iterate_lines(text):
        match = None if in_code else _HEADING.match(line)
        if match:
            level = len(match.group(1)) + levels
            level = max(1, min(level, _MAXIMUM_HEADING_LEVEL))
            lines.append('#' * level + line[match.end():])
        else:
            lines.append(line)
    return '\n'.join(lines)

def split_front_matter(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
    """Separates the YAML front matter from markdown `text`.

    Front matter must start on the first line that is not blank. It opens with
    '---' (and closes with '---' or '...') or opens and closes with "'''".

    Args:
        text: markdown text that may start with front matter.

    Returns:
        The front matter as a `dict` (which is empty if there is no front
            matter) and the rest of `text`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if the front matter is never closed or is not a mapping of
            keys to values.

    """
    lines = text.lstrip('﻿').splitlines()
    start = 0
    while start < len(lines) and not lines[start].strip():
        start += 1
    if start == len(lines):
        return {}, ''
    opener = lines[start].strip()
    if opener not in _FRONT_MATTER_DELIMITERS:
        return {}, text
    closers = _FRONT_MATTER_DELIMITERS[opener]
    for end in range(start + 1, len(lines)):
        if lines[end].strip() in closers:
            break
    else:
        message = f'front matter opened with "{opener}" is never closed'
        raise ValueError(message)
    metadata = yaml.safe_load('\n'.join(lines[start + 1:end]))
    if metadata is None:
        metadata = {}
    if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
        message = 'front matter must be a mapping of keys to values'
        raise ValueError(message)  # noqa: TRY004
    return metadata, '\n'.join(lines[end + 1:])

def split_sections(
        text: str,
        names: dict[str, str],
        default: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Divides markdown `text` into the sections marked by dividers.

    A divider is a line with only a section name inside '<' and '>' (such as
    '<slides>'). The text after a divider, up to the next divider, belongs to
    that section. Text before the first divider belongs to the `default`
    section. A closing divider (such as '</slides>') returns to the `default`
    section. Dividers inside fenced code blocks are ignored. If a section
    appears more than once, its parts are joined in order.

    Args:
        text: markdown text without front matter.
        names: `dict` with keys that are the names that may appear in dividers
            (in lower case) and values that are the sections they mark. This
            allows more than one name for a section (such as 'manuscript' for
            'text').
        default: the section for text that is not after a divider.

    Returns:
        A `dict` with keys that are section names and values that are the
            stripped text of each section. Only sections with text are included.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a divider names a section that is not in `names`.

    """
    parts: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    current = default
    for line, in_code in _iterate_lines(text):
        match = None if in_code else _DIVIDER.match(line)
        if match:
            closing, name = match.groups()
            if name.lower() not in names:
                known = ', '.join(f'<{key}>' for key in names)
                message = f'unknown divider "{line.strip()}" (use {known})'
                raise ValueError(message)
            current = default if closing else names[name.lower()]
            parts.setdefault(current, []).append('')
            continue
        parts.setdefault(current, []).append(line)
    sections = {}
    for name, lines in parts.items():
        section = '\n'.join(lines).strip('\n')
        if section.strip():
            sections[name] = section
    return sections

docs.title: outline
docs.text:
The structure of a coursebook project.

An outline is a list of labeled titles, such as:

I: Introduction
II: The Problem
A: History
1: Early Cases
2: Modern Cases
B: Current Law
III: Conclusion

The level of each entry comes from its label instead of from indentation. A label can be an upper case Roman numeral (I), an upper case letter (A), an Arabic number (1), a lower case letter (a), or a lower case Roman numeral (i). An entry is placed:

  1. after the deepest earlier entry whose next label it is (so 'B' follows 'A'); or, if there is none,
  2. beneath the previous entry if it is the first label of a kind that is not used by the previous entry or its parents (so 'A' or '1' opens a new level); or, if neither applies,
  3. after the deepest earlier entry with the same kind of label, even if some labels were skipped (so 'C' can follow 'A'), with a warning.

Because of the first rule, 'i' after 'h' continues the lower case letters instead of starting lower case Roman numerals.

An entry without a number (such as a preface or an appendix) has a label of dashes: '-' for the top level, '--' for the level below it, and so on. An unnumbered entry takes the place of a numbered one in the outline, so the numbering continues after it. A numbered label that opens a new level after an unnumbered entry is placed at the level of the unnumbered entry instead of beneath it.

Each entry is matched to the source file named after its title. To use another file, add it after a '|' (the file name must end with '.md'):

I: Introduction | chapters/intro.md
Contents

Outline: the entries of a project in order. OutlineEntry: a single entry in an outline. OutlineLine: type of an outline line or a tuple of its parts. parse_outline_line: splits an outline line into its label, title, and file. _LABEL_KINDS: the kinds of labels that may be used in an outline, each with a function that creates a label from a number and a function that returns the number of a label (or None). _LOGGER: logger for warnings about skipped labels. _Stack: type of the open entries while an outline is read. _ROMAN_NUMERALS: Roman numeral symbols and their values.

@classmethod
def from_lines(cls, lines: Iterable[OutlineLine]) -> Outline:
    """Creates an outline from labeled lines.

    Args:
        lines: each item is either a line from an outline (such as
            'A: History') or a `tuple` of a label, a title, and
            (optionally) a file. Blank lines are skipped.

    Returns:
        An outline with the level of each entry set from its label.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a line has no label or title, or if a label cannot
            be placed in the outline.

    """
    outline = cls()
    # The last item is the most recent entry.
    stack: _Stack = []
    for line in lines:
        if isinstance(line, str):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            label, title, file = parse_outline_line(line)
        else:
            label, title, file = _parse_parts(line)
        if _is_unnumbered(label):
            depth, kind, number = _place_unnumbered(label, title, stack)
            label = ''
        else:
            depth, kind, number = _place_label(label, stack)
        entry = OutlineEntry(
            label = label, title = title, level = depth, file = file)
        del stack[depth:]
        if depth == 0:
            outline.entries.append(entry)
        else:
            stack[-1][0].children.append(entry)
        stack.append((entry, kind, number))
    return outline

def parse_outline_line(line: str) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
    """Splits a line from an outline into its label, title, and file.

    The label and title may be separated by ':' or '=' (the same separators
    allowed in an `ini` file). A file may follow the title after a '|'.

    Args:
        line: a line from an outline (such as 'A: History' or
            'A: History | history_notes.md').

    Returns:
        The label (without any trailing period or surrounding parentheses),
            the title, and the file (or `None`).

    Raises:
        ValueError: if `line` does not have both a label and a title.

    """
    positions = [line.find(mark) for mark in ':=' if mark in line]
    if not positions:
        message = f'outline line "{line.strip()}" needs a label and a title'
        raise ValueError(message)
    split = min(positions)
    return _parse_parts((line[:split], line[split + 1:]), line)

def build(
        self,
        include: Iterable[str] | None = None,
        output_folder: _PathLike | None = None) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Creates the files for the sections of the project.

    Each section is exported to every format set for it (such as Word and
    PDF). The files are exported at the same time, each in its own pandoc
    process.

    Args:
        include: the sections to create files for. Defaults to `None`,
            which uses `include`.
        output_folder: folder for the created files. Defaults to `None`,
            which uses `output_folder`.

    Returns:
        The paths to the created files, in the order of `include` and then
            of the formats of each section.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if a template, bibliography, or CSL file is not
            found.
        ImportError: if a format needs a package that is not installed.
        ValueError: if a section, format, or template is not valid, or a
            format cannot hold a section.
        RuntimeError: if pandoc fails.

    """
    sections = settings.normalize_sections(
        self.include if include is None else include)
    folder = (
        self.output_folder if output_folder is None
        else self._resolve(output_folder))
    for entry in self.missing:
        _LOGGER.warning(
            'No source file "%s" for outline entry "%s"',
            entry.file_name, entry.title)
    folder.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    stem = markdown.normalize_name(self.settings.name) or 'coursebook'
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        jobs = []
        for section in sections:
            text = self.assemble(section)
            for name in self.settings.formats_for(section):
                exporter = exporters.get_exporter(name)
                if section not in exporter.sections:
                    message = (
                        f'the {section} cannot be exported to {name} '
                        f'(use {", ".join(_formats_for(section))})')
                    raise ValueError(message)
                options = self._get_options(
                    section, exporter, pathlib.Path(temporary))
                path = folder / (
                    f'{stem}{_SUFFIXES[section]}.{exporter.extension}')
                jobs.append((exporter, text, path, options))
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as pool:
            futures = [pool.submit(job[0].export, *job[1:]) for job in jobs]
            return [future.result() for future in futures]

def create_project(
        folder: str | pathlib.Path,
        name: str | None = None,
        style: str = 'coursebook',
        outline_lines: Iterable[outline.OutlineLine] | None = None,
        file_format: str = 'ini') -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Creates a project folder with a project file and source files.

    Each outline entry gets a source file with a divider for each section of
    the style. Source files that already exist are left alone. If two entries
    would share a source file (because they have the same title), the later
    one is given its own file in the outline.

    Args:
        folder: the project folder, which is created if it does not exist.
        name: the title of the project. Defaults to `None`, which uses the
            name of `folder` in title case, with spaces for underscores and
            dashes.
        style: the name of the style. Defaults to 'coursebook'.
        outline_lines: the outline of the project. Defaults to `None`, which
            uses a short sample outline.
        file_format: the format of the project file ('ini', 'toml', or
            'yaml'). Defaults to 'ini'.

    Returns:
        The paths to the files and folders that were created.

    Raises:
        FileExistsError: if `folder` already has a project file.
        ValueError: if the style, outline, or file format is not valid.

    """
    folder = pathlib.Path(folder)
    if file_format not in PROJECT_FILE_FORMATS:
        message = (
            f'unknown project file format "{file_format}" (use '
            f'{", ".join(PROJECT_FILE_FORMATS)})')
        raise ValueError(message)
    try:
        existing = settings.find_project_file(folder)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    else:
        message = f'{folder} already has a project file ({existing.name})'
        raise FileExistsError(message)
    project_style = styles.get_style(style)
    project_outline = outline.Outline.from_lines(
        list(outline_lines) if outline_lines else _DEFAULT_OUTLINE)
    _give_entries_own_files(project_outline)
    if not name:
        words = folder.resolve().name.replace('_', ' ').replace('-', ' ')
        name = string.capwords(words) or 'Untitled'
    folder.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    project_file = folder / f'project.{file_format}'
    project_file.write_text(
        _format_project_file(name, style, project_outline, file_format),
        encoding = 'utf-8')
    created = [project_file]
    skeleton = '\n\n\n'.join(
        f'<{section}>' for section in project_style.sections) + '\n'
    for entry in project_outline:
        path = folder / entry.file_name
        if path.exists():
            continue
        path.parent.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
        path.write_text(skeleton, encoding = 'utf-8')
        created.append(path)
    visuals = folder / 'visuals'
    if not visuals.exists():
        visuals.mkdir()
        created.append(visuals)
    return created

def write_template(
        style: str,
        destination: str | pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Writes the Word or PowerPoint template of a style.

    The template can be changed in Word or PowerPoint and then named in the
    "Text Template" or "Slides Template" setting of a project.

    Args:
        style: the name of the style.
        destination: path for the template. Its extension ('.docx' or
            '.pptx') chooses which template is written.

    Returns:
        The path to the template.

    Raises:
        FileExistsError: if `destination` already exists.
        ValueError: if the style or extension is not valid.

    """
    destination = pathlib.Path(destination)
    suffix = destination.suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in {'.docx', '.pptx'}:
        message = f'{destination.name} must end with .docx or .pptx'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if destination.exists():
        message = f'{destination} already exists'
        raise FileExistsError(message)
    project_style = styles.get_style(style)
    destination.parent.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    if suffix == '.docx':
        name = project_style.text_template
        if name is None:
            return templates.create_word_template(
                project_style.formatting, destination)
        application = 'word'
    else:
        name = project_style.slides_template
        if name is None:
            destination.write_bytes(templates.get_pandoc_template('pptx'))
            return destination
        application = 'powerpoint'
    found = templates.find_template(
        name, application = application, folder = pathlib.Path.cwd())
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
        prepared = templates.prepare_template(found, temporary)
        shutil.copyfile(prepared, destination)
    return destination

@classmethod
def from_mapping(
        cls,
        mapping: Mapping[str, Any],
        infer_types: bool = False) -> Settings:
    """Creates settings from a `dict` of options.

    Args:
        mapping: options with names as they appear in a project file (such
            as 'Output Folder').
        infer_types: whether to convert `str` values to other types (such
            as `bool` or `list`). This should be `True` for `ini` files,
            which only store `str` values. Defaults to `False`.

    Returns:
        Settings with the options in `mapping`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if a setting has a value of the wrong type or
            `include` names an unknown section.

    """
    fields = {field.name: field for field in dataclasses.fields(cls)}
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
    extras: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for key, value in mapping.items():
        name = markdown.normalize_name(str(key))
        name = _SETTING_ALIASES.get(name, name)
        if name not in fields or name == 'extras':
            extras[name] = camina.typify(value) if infer_types else value
            continue
        kwargs[name] = _convert_setting(name, value, fields[name].type)
    return cls(**kwargs, extras = extras)

def find_project_file(folder: str | pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns the path to the project file in `folder`.

    Args:
        folder: the project folder.

    Returns:
        The path to the project file.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if `folder` does not exist or has no project file.
        ValueError: if `folder` has more than one project file.

    """
    folder = pathlib.Path(folder)
    if not folder.is_dir():
        message = f'project folder {folder} does not exist'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    names = {path.name.lower(): path for path in folder.iterdir()}
    found = [names[name] for name in PROJECT_FILE_NAMES if name in names]
    if not found:
        message = (
            f'no project file in {folder} (expected one of: '
            f'{", ".join(PROJECT_FILE_NAMES)})')
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    if len(found) > 1:
        listed = ', '.join(path.name for path in found)
        message = f'{folder} has more than one project file ({listed})'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return found[0]

    """Converts section names (and their aliases) to their standard names.

    normalized: list[str] = []

def read_project_file(
        path: str | pathlib.Path) -> tuple[Settings, outline.Outline]:
    """Returns the settings and outline in a project file.

    Args:
        path: path to an `ini`, `toml`, `yaml`, or `yml` project file.

    Returns:
        The settings from the "Project" section and the outline from the
            "Outline" section.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if `path` is not a file.
        ValueError: if the file type is not supported or the contents are not
            valid.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        message = f'project file {path} not found'
        raise FileNotFoundError(message)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == '.ini':
        options, lines = _read_ini(path)
        settings = Settings.from_mapping(options, infer_types = True)
    elif suffix in {'.toml', '.yaml', '.yml'}:
        options, lines = _read_structured(path)
        settings = Settings.from_mapping(options)
    else:
        message = f'{path.name} is not an ini, toml, or yaml file'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return settings, outline.Outline.from_lines(lines)

def load_sources(folder: str | pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Source]:
    """Loads every markdown file in `folder`.

    Subfolders are not searched.

    Args:
        folder: the project folder.

    Returns:
        A `dict` with keys that are the names of the sources (see
            `markdown.normalize_name`) and values that are the sources.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if two files have the same normalized name (such as
            'Introduction.md' and 'introduction.md') or a file is not valid.

    """
    sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
    for path in sorted(pathlib.Path(folder).glob('*.md')):
        source = Source.from_file(path)
        if source.name in sources:
            other = sources[source.name].path
            name = other.name if other else source.name
            message = f'{path.name} and {name} are for the same outline entry'
            raise ValueError(message)
        sources[source.name] = source
    return sources

def get_style(name: str, **overrides: Any) -> Style:
    """Returns the style with `name`.

    Args:
        name: the name of a `Style` subclass or one of its aliases (such as
            'law review' or 'Coursebook').
        **overrides: values that replace the defaults of the style. Values
            of `None` are ignored.

    Returns:
        An instance of the style.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if no style has `name`.

    """
    key = markdown.normalize_name(name)
    choices: dict[str, type[Style]] = {}
    for registered_name, registered in Style.registry.items():
        choices[str(registered_name)] = registered
        for alias in registered.aliases:
            choices.setdefault(alias, registered)
    choices.pop('style', None)
    if key not in choices:
        known = ', '.join(sorted(choices))
        message = f'unknown style "{name}" (use one of: {known})'
        raise ValueError(message)
    kwargs = {
        field: value for field, value in overrides.items()
        if value is not None}
    return choices[key](**kwargs)

Finds and prepares the templates and citation styles used for exports.

Pandoc formats Word and PowerPoint files by copying the styles of a reference document (a '.docx' or '.pptx' file). This module turns the templates that a project names into reference documents:

  • Word: '.docx' files are used as is and '.dotx' templates are converted. If a project does not name a Word template, pandoc's default template is used with the Formatting of the style applied.
  • PowerPoint: '.pptx' files are used as is and '.potx' templates and '.thmx' Office themes are converted.

Citation Style Language ('.csl') files are found the same way as templates.

A template is found by its path (relative to the project folder) or by its name. A name is looked for first in the project folder and then among the templates included with coursebook (such as 'chalkboard' and 'bluebook-law-review').

create_word_template: creates a Word reference document with formatting. find_template: returns the path to a template. get_pandoc_template: returns pandoc's default reference document. list_templates: returns the names of the included templates. prepare_template: converts a template into a reference document. _DOCUMENT: the start of the Word content types. _EXTENSIONS: the template file extensions for each kind of template. _HEADING_STYLES: the Word styles that are formatted as headings. _MAIN_CONTENT_TYPES: the content types that templates are converted from and to. _PRESENTATION: the start of the PowerPoint content types. _PRESENTATION_NAMESPACES: the XML namespaces of PowerPoint parts. _RELATIONSHIPS: the namespace of Office relationship types. _TEMPLATES_FOLDER: folder with the templates included with coursebook. _THEME_EXTRA_PARTS: the parts that a presentation needs but an Office theme does not include. _XML_DECLARATION: the declaration at the start of each XML part.

def find_template(
        name: str,
        application: str,
        folder: str | pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Returns the path to the template for `name`.

    Args:
        name: a path to a template (absolute or relative to `folder`) or the
            name of a template without its extension.
        application: 'word', 'powerpoint', or 'csl'.
        folder: the project folder.

    Returns:
        The path to the template.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: if no template is found for `name`.
        ValueError: if `application` is not 'word', 'powerpoint', or 'csl' or
            the template has the wrong extension.

    """
    if application not in _EXTENSIONS:
        message = f'unknown application "{application}"'
        raise ValueError(message)
    extensions = _EXTENSIONS[application]
    path = pathlib.Path(folder) / pathlib.Path(name).expanduser()
    if path.suffix:
        if path.suffix.lower() not in extensions:
            message = (
                f'{path.name} is not a {application} template (use '
                f'{", ".join(extensions)})')
            raise ValueError(message)
        if path.is_file():
            return path
    else:
        for base in (pathlib.Path(folder), _TEMPLATES_FOLDER / application):
            for extension in extensions:
                candidate = base / f'{name}{extension}'
                if candidate.is_file():
                    return candidate
    included = ', '.join(list_templates(application)) or 'none'
    message = (
        f'{application} template "{name}" not found (included templates: '
        f'{included})')
    raise FileNotFoundError(message)

        check = True)

def list_templates(application: str) -> list[str]:
    """Returns the names of the templates included with `coursebook`.

    Args:
        application: 'word', 'powerpoint', or 'csl'.

    Returns:
        The names of the included templates, without their extensions.

    """
    folder = _TEMPLATES_FOLDER / application
    if not folder.is_dir():
        return []
    extensions = _EXTENSIONS.get(application, ())
    return sorted(
        path.stem for path in folder.iterdir()
        if path.suffix.lower() in extensions)

def prepare_template(
        path: str | pathlib.Path,
        destination: str | pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    """Converts a template into a reference document that pandoc can use.

    Args:
        path: path to a '.docx', '.dotx', '.pptx', '.potx', or '.thmx' file.
        destination: folder for a converted template.

    Returns:
        `path` if it is already a '.docx' or '.pptx' file. Otherwise, the
            path to the converted template in `destination`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if `path` does not have a supported extension.

    """
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in {'.docx', '.pptx'}:
        return path
    extension = '.docx' if suffix == '.dotx' else '.pptx'
    destination = pathlib.Path(destination)
    destination.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)
    converted = destination / f'{path.stem}{extension}'
    if suffix in _MAIN_CONTENT_TYPES:
        _convert_office_template(path, converted)
    elif suffix == '.thmx':
        _convert_theme(path, converted)
    else:
        message = f'{path.name} is not a Word or PowerPoint template'
        raise ValueError(message)
    return converted
